title: Wipro Merges VLSI Design Subsidiary Into IT Services Arm
excerpt: Wipro has merged its US chip-design subsidiary, formerly Eximius Design, into its IT services entity effective October 1, 2026, continuing its drive to simplify the group structure. There is no cash consideration and no change in shareholding.
body:
• The transaction: Wipro has completed the merger of its US step-down subsidiary Wipro VLSI Design Services, LLC into Wipro IT Services, LLC, effective October 1, 2026 (Eastern Time), with the company informing stock exchanges on October 3.
  • The numbers: The VLSI design unit reported turnover of $1,043,971 as of March 31, 2026, against nil turnover for the IT services entity — a revenue-generating unit folded into a non-revenue one within the same wholly owned group.
  • No impact on investors' holdings: There is no cash consideration and no share exchange, so the shareholding pattern of the listed entity does not change.
  • The rationale: Wipro says the move is aimed at rationalizing and consolidating the overall group structure, cutting administrative overheads and reducing the multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances.

Wipro Limited has completed the merger of Wipro VLSI Design Services, LLC into Wipro IT Services, LLC, both step-down subsidiaries in the United States. The transaction became effective on October 1, 2026, Eastern Time, and the company informed the BSE, NSE and NYSE on October 3, 2026, pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

The details

The absorbed entity, Wipro VLSI Design Services, LLC — formerly Eximius Design LLC — operates in VLSI design, verification, physical and analog design, FPGA and product engineering. It reported turnover of $1,043,971 for the year ended March 31, 2026. The surviving entity, Wipro IT Services, LLC, reported nil turnover for the same period. Because both entities are wholly owned subsidiaries and the deal involves no cash consideration and no share exchange ratio, Wipro stated there will be no change in the shareholding pattern of the listed entity.

The disclosure notes the transaction does not fall under related-party transactions requiring arm's-length pricing disclosures. In substance, the merger folds a small but revenue-generating semiconductor design unit into a broader software development entity under the same corporate roof — consolidating specialized chip-design capabilities with the IT services umbrella.

Context and background

The move continues a multi-year simplification drive. Wipro acquired Silicon Valley-based Eximius Design around 2020 to build a foothold in the semiconductor industry, folding its engineering talent — roughly 1,100 employees across the US, India and Malaysia at the time — into its EngineeringNXT framework. In October 2023, Wipro's board approved merging five Indian wholly owned subsidiaries into the parent, citing the same four reasons repeated now: consolidating business operations, enabling synergies, reducing administrative and managerial overheads, and optimizing the legal entity structure. Wipro's CFO at the time, Aparna Iyer, described that exercise as "only for administrative convenience."

The latest US-side merger follows the same logic at the overseas-entity level: fewer legal entities means fewer parallel compliances, audits and administrative costs, without altering the consolidated financial position.

"The transaction became effective on October 1, 2026, Eastern Time, with the company receiving formal intimation on October 3, 2026."

— Wipro's exchange filing on the merger completion

Impact and analysis

For Wipro's operating profile, the direct financial effect is negligible — about $1 million in annual turnover is immaterial against the company's scale, and consolidation does not change group revenue. The significance is structural and strategic: placing chip-design capabilities inside the IT services entity positions Wipro to sell semiconductor design bundled with broader software development offerings to enterprise clients, at a time when the semiconductor ecosystem is expanding beyond traditional chipmakers into cloud, hyperscale, automotive and consumer electronics.

The timing is worth noting. Wipro's stock has been under pressure — down roughly 33% over the past year per market data — and the company has been pruning and consolidating, including completing the acquisition of select Alpha Net Consulting customer contracts on the same effective date of October 1, 2026. Investors tend to read sustained entity rationalization as management attention on cost discipline, even when individual transactions are small.

Diaspora angle

Wipro is NYSE-listed and widely held by Indian-American retail investors, who watch its corporate actions as a barometer of the Indian IT sector. The merger also touches a diaspora talent story: the absorbed unit traces back to Eximius Design, founded by an Indian immigrant engineer in Silicon Valley in 2013 — a reminder of how diaspora-founded semiconductor expertise has been folded into India's IT majors.

What's next

The administrative consolidation is complete; the operational test is whether the unified US entity wins semiconductor-adjacent work bundled with software services. Watch Wipro's coming quarters for commentary on its engineering-services pipeline and whether the rationalized structure shows up as margin discipline in its US operations.
